title: The Most Profitable AI Business You've Never Heard Of
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The speaker says he has an affiliate link for Beehiiv and actively uses it, but had never tried Beehiiv Communities before the recording. The agency results are hypothetical projections, not reported client outcomes.

stated_problem.quote: Speaking from experience, a big email list does not automatically turn into revenue.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: AI email list monetization agency
idea.one_liner: Help business owners use AI and their existing email lists to reactivate subscribers and generate revenue, charging a monthly fee or possibly making payment contingent on results.
idea.customer: Business owners with email lists, including local service businesses.
idea.offer: Use AI and email platform data to segment subscribers, invite engaged members to a community, and run reactivation campaigns.
idea.revenue_model: The speaker suggests $1,000 per month, while also pitching a no-risk arrangement where the client pays only if revenue is generated; the exact fee structure is unclear.

key_quotes.quote: You don't think that business owner would pay you $1,000 a month to generate $12,000 a month for them?
Speaking from experience, a big email list does not automatically turn into revenue.
You don't think that business owner would pay you $1,000 a month to generate $12,000 a month for them.

claims.quote: That would be a 12x return on investment that they paying you.

claims.claim: He estimates about 50 of those people are business owners.
claims.quote: How many of those are business owners? About 50.

claims.claim: He says 50 potential contacts could become 100 through referrals.
claims.quote: And then the 50 becomes a hundred because of referrals because one person that's thrilled usually refers multiple, not just one.

claims.claim: He says there are 33 million business owners in America and 400 million worldwide.

claims.claim: He proposes that clients could pay nothing unless the service generates revenue.

acquisition_channels.details: Start with business owners the founder or client already knows and use referrals from satisfied clients.
The speaker says ads can be used to find clients.
He suggests posting in Facebook groups for local communities and on Reddit.

ideas.delivery: The agency reviews the client's email list and engagement data, segments subscribers, and runs email reactivation or community-invitation campaigns with AI tools and the client's email platform. The client supplies list access and may approve emails or campaign actions.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply to subscriber data and email marketing. The client and agency need appropriate data-processing terms, a valid basis for marketing, required notices, and opt-out handling.

stated_problem.quote: Both are great, but they're completely disconnected from each other.

idea.name: Newsletter with paid community
idea.one_liner: Chris Koerner runs a large newsletter alongside a paid community, using content and social channels to bring readers into a connected membership.
idea.customer: Newsletter readers and members interested in the speaker's business content.
idea.offer: A newsletter plus a community with discussions and member interaction.
idea.revenue_model: Paid community memberships; the transcript does not state the membership price or revenue.

key_quotes.quote: I have about 273,000 people on my newsletter.
And then I also have a paid community.
Both are great, but they're completely disconnected from each other.

claims.claim: The speaker says he has used Beehiiv for over two years.
claims.quote: I've used Beehive for over 2 years.

claims.claim: He says Substack takes 10% and Beehiiv takes 0%.
claims.quote: Remember, Substack takes 10% of everything. Behive takes 0%.

acquisition_channels.details: The speaker lists his podcast, social media, YouTube, and Instagram as audience sources.
The newsletter is another audience source and can invite readers into the community.

ideas.delivery: The speaker publishes a newsletter and provides a paid online community for members to discuss its content and interact.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply to subscriber data and email invitations. Paid consumer memberships should have clear subscription terms and cancellation information; the DMCC Act may apply.

idea.name: Niche online community
idea.one_liner: Create a free, paid, or free-to-paid online community around a niche, with member discussions, content, events, and shared accountability.
idea.customer: People interested in a defined topic or shared goal, such as entrepreneurs or appliance-rental business starters.
idea.offer: An online community with channels, discussions, events, and member interaction.
idea.revenue_model: Free access, paid access, or a free community with paid channels; no specific price is stated.

key_quotes.quote: It's a marketplace two-sided. You need readers and you need writers. You need people to engage with each other because if someone checks out the community and it looks dead, they're gone.

So, everything I just showed you was done with the intent to help you start a business, a community business using either uh the Beehive MCP through your favorite AI tool or just using Beehive Community directly

claims.claim: The speaker recommends seeding a community with 10 to 20 founding members.
claims.quote: Seed 10 to 20 founding members by hand.

claims.claim: He recommends three to five easy questions for new members.
claims.quote: See three to five questions anyone can answer without feeling dumb.

claims.claim: He recommends keeping the community to three or four channels at most.
claims.quote: Keep channels to three to or four max.

claims.claim: He suggests starting with five or six channels and later reducing them to two or three.
claims.quote: you might even want to add five to six channels and then just know in a month or three you're going to cut that down to two to three

claims.claim: He recommends replying to every comment for the first 14 days.
claims.quote: you reply to every single comment for the first 14 days.

acquisition_channels.details: Invite existing newsletter subscribers into the community; the speaker says a newsletter is a lower-stakes way to build an audience first.

ideas.delivery: The owner sets up channels, posts, events, onboarding, and community rituals on an online platform. Members discuss topics, share content, and interact; the owner or a community manager encourages participation.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply if the community uses an email list or processes member data. Paid consumer memberships should have clear subscription terms and cancellation information; the DMCC Act may apply.

idea.name: Sell an AI email-list monetization skill
idea.one_liner: Package the demonstrated email-list workflow as a reusable AI skill and sell it to people who want to monetize email lists.
idea.customer: People or business owners who want to improve email-list monetization.
idea.offer: A reusable AI skill based on a workflow for analyzing and monetizing an email list.
idea.revenue_model: Sell the skill through an online marketplace; no price is stated.

key_quotes.quote: you can convert that entire chat window into a skill that you can sell, put on a marketplace

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that one simple sentence can be used to turn the chat into a sellable skill.
claims.quote: with one simple sentence, you can convert that entire chat window into a skill that you can sell

acquisition_channels.details: The speaker suggests listing the skill on a marketplace but does not name one.

ideas.delivery: Create a reusable AI skill from the demonstrated chat workflow and distribute it as a digital product.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If sold to UK consumers, digital-content terms and consumer protection rules apply. UK GDPR applies if the product processes personal data from email lists.

stated_problem.quote: So if your friend owns a plumbing business, surely his email list isn't going to want to join a community and talk about their plumbing issues together.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Local newsletter from a plumbing customer list
idea.one_liner: Help a plumbing business use its customer email list to launch a local newsletter or community for people in the same city.
idea.customer: Local residents on a plumbing business's existing email list.
idea.offer: A local newsletter or community built around the shared city rather than plumbing topics.

key_quotes.quote: But all of those people live in the same city and local newsletters are one of the best newsletter concepts right now.
So what's stopping you from helping your plumbing business owner friend from launching a local newsletter off the back of his email list?

acquisition_channels.details: Use the plumbing business's existing email list to invite local residents.

ideas.delivery: The plumbing business owner or a helper launches and runs a local newsletter or online community for the people on the list.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply to using customer addresses and emailing residents. Use the list only with an appropriate lawful basis and marketing permissions, provide required notices, and honor opt-outs.
